subject: Re: MAP draft — Technical evaluation plan (latency/cost targets, model shortlist)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sabrina Lee <sabrina.lee@acmecorp.com>, Rajiv Patel <rpatel@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft — Technical evaluation plan (post-call recap)

Hi Sabrina / Rajiv,

Thanks again for the productive call earlier — great context on Acme's search and product-recommendation flows. As discussed, attached is the first draft of the Mutual Action Plan (ACME MAP v1) with a focused milestone for the technical evaluation. Please see the summary below and the proposed responsibilities / dates in the attachment.

Quick summary of the Technical Evaluation milestone (high level):
- Goal: Validate model quality, latency, and per-unit cost for production traffic patterns for the recommendations use case.
- Success criteria (benchmarks we can agree on):
  * Latency: p95 generation latency <= 150 ms for 256-token requests in our test harness
  * Cost: average model-inference spend <= $0.10 per 1k tokens (after batching/quantization)
  * Quality: top-K NDCG >= 0.78 vs your ground-truth scoring on the 10k eval set; embedding cosine similarity > 0.92 for known paraphrase pairs
- Model shortlist: Llama-3-70B (quantized 4-bit), Mistral-Instruct-70B, and the Redwood-verified distilled variant (rwd-distill-13B). We propose running the same evaluation across all three to compare cost/latency/quality tradeoffs.

Proposed responsibilities / milestones (see attached MAP sheet for row-level ownership):
- Acme (Sabrina / Rajiv): provide a 10k sample eval set + representative inference load profile by 2027-05-09. Provide access to a minimal staging dataset and confirm the acceptance criteria for NDCG.
- Redwood (Camila + infra): provision a temporary test endpoint, supply the benchmark harness (redwood_benchmark_template.xlsx + scripts), and run the initial runs by 2027-05-16. Share raw logs and aggregated p95/p50, token counts, and cost estimates.
- Joint: run two rounds (initial + tuned) with parameter sweeps (quantization, batch size, KV cache settings) and agree on a recommended model and configuration by 2027-05-30.

Dependencies: procurement of a short-term dedicated instance if Acme wants consistent throughput for QA (procurement dependency; Rajiv to confirm). Also need NDA addendum signed for access to the staging data (if not covered).

Next steps I propose:
1) Sabrina / Rajiv confirm the sample set availability and ownership by EOD 2027-05-05.
2) Camila will send the benchmark harness and a short runbook today.
3) We lock the target "MAP technical milestone close" date as 2027-05-30 (we can adjust if procurement pushes).

Attached: ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx (milestones/responsibilities) and redwood_benchmark_template.xlsx (run instructions + expected outputs).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 15-min sync if useful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0142

From: Sabrina Lee <sabrina.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Rajiv Patel <rpatel@acme.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft — Technical evaluation plan (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap and the clear milestones. A few notes from our side:

- The 10k eval set is doable; our SRE/analytics team needs a pointer to the schema for the sample. We'll aim to deliver by 2027-05-09 as requested.
- For latency, p95 <=150ms sounds aggressive but reasonable as a target for the optimized path. We will flag any outliers for the cold-start path.
- Procurement: short-term dedicated instance is possible but Rajiv needs to confirm cost center approval. That might add a 1-2 week delay if procurement needs PO.

Action items from Acme:
- Sabrina: share eval set schema and PO owner by 2027-05-05.
- Rajiv: confirm procurement timeline and flag any constraints by 2027-05-07.

One question on the model shortlist: can Redwood add a managed LLM that is more inference-cost optimized (e.g., a tuned rwd-distill-13B) to the comparison? If it meets quality thresholds that would be preferred for go-live cost reasons.

Thanks,
Sabrina
Head of Search & Recommendations | Acme Corp
Sabrina.Lee@acmecorp.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sabrina Lee <sabrina.lee@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rpatel@acme.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft — Technical evaluation plan (benchmarks + harness)

Hi Sabrina / team,

Thanks — quick technical follow-up. I attached the benchmark harness (redwood_benchmark_template.xlsx) and a short runbook. A couple of clarifications that will help the runs produce comparable numbers:

- Test harness config: please include representative prompt mix (prod: 60% short queries < 64 tokens, 30% mid 64-256, 10% long >256). We'll use the same mix across all model runs.
- Latency measurement: our p95 numbers assume warmed KV cache and steady-state traffic; cold-start/resident eviction cases will be documented separately.
- Cost calc: we'll include amortized GPU cost + token compute; you should expect per-1k-token estimates in the output tab.

Proposed bench parameters (defaults):
- batch_size: 8 (we'll sweep 4-16)
- quant: 4-bit asymmetric (try 8-bit for baseline)
- concurrency: 12 concurrent requests for the initial run

I've added rwd-distill-13B to the shortlist in the attached MAP (lightweight variant we can run quickly). We'll also run a fallback path on a smaller open model if cost constraints are binding.

I'll schedule an initial shared session to walk your engineers through the harness on 2027-05-06 at 10:00 AM PST — let me know if that works.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai

From: Rajiv Patel <rpatel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sabrina Lee <sabrina.lee@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft — Technical evaluation plan (procurement note)

Quick update from procurement side:

- PO owner confirmed (finance contact: J. Alvarez). Short-term dedicated instance request approved in principle but needs a cost estimate and a purchase request by 2027-05-12. If Redwood can provide an estimated cost range for a 2-week dedicated instance for the benchmark runs (GPU type + expected bill), we can expedite.
- Otherwise, we'll start with shared hosted runs per Camila's harness and escalate to dedicated if we see variance in the p95 results.

I'll coordinate with Sabrina to get the eval set schema to you no later than 2027-05-05.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Director of Engineering | Acme Corp
rpatel@acme.com
